route.title: Vision report heading
route.marker: The revelation-and-prophet report formula completes before direct lament and the how-long question begin at 1:2.
route.rationale: The title remains recoverable as a formal threshold while requiring the dialogue it governs for interpretation.
route.rejected: Merge 1:1 into the 1:2-4 complaint and blur the heading-to-lament transition.
route.counter: The heading governs the whole book and is too thin for context-free interpretation.
route.basis: A complete report heading is distinct from the following direct address; mandatory 1:1-2:5 hydration prevents authorship or dating overreach.
route.guard: Do not treat genre or prophet-identification wording as authorship, date, canon, or historical authority.

route.title: First how-long complaint
route.marker: How-long and why questions move through violence and strife to the doubled therefore-result in paralyzed instruction and perverted justice at 1:4.
route.rationale: Cry, witnessed disorder, and judicial result form one causal complaint before the imperative answer opens at 1:5.
route.rejected: Split 1:4 as an independent law-and-justice maxim or surface 1:2-3 apart from its result.
route.counter: Verse 1:4 has aphoristic wording and strong isolated-retrieval pressure.
route.basis: The discourse particles in 1:4 bind its memorable conclusion backward to 1:2-3, so the full lament is the defensible surface.
route.guard: Never retrieve 1:4 without the 1:2-4 complaint and the larger dialogue context.

route.title: Divine answer announcing the Chaldean force
route.marker: Plural look-watch-wonder imperatives open the answer, 1:6 names its instrument, and the cumulative force catalogue reaches a guilt verdict at 1:11.
route.rationale: Announcement, named agent, military characteristics, violence, conquest, and final culpability resolve as one divine-answer movement.
route.rejected: Detach 1:5, split 1:5-6 from 1:7-11, or surface catalogue fragments.
route.counter: Verse 1:6 is a strong naming turn and 1:11 shifts from description to evaluation.
route.basis: The naming and verdict are the opening and closing functions of one answer; internal turns remain searchable only with the complete movement.
route.guard: Acts 13 reception of 1:5 is later context only and cannot authorize a Habakkuk boundary or fulfillment claim.

route.title: Renewed address and devouring-agent complaint
route.marker: Renewed direct address and the why-question develop through fish, hook, net, sacrifice, prosperity, and the final mercy question; a WLC-family samekh follows 1:17.
route.rationale: The difficult premise in 1:12 and the concrete net imagery jointly build the second complaint, which closes before the watchpost posture.
route.rejected: Split 1:12-13 from 1:14-17, isolate 1:12, or extend the complaint through 2:1.
route.counter: The 1:12 wording is textually difficult and fish imagery turns sharply at 1:14.
route.basis: Direct address, repeated interrogation, image development, and final question outweigh the internal imagery turn; no preferred reading is selected.
route.guard: The correlated local reading at 1:12 is boundary-neutral; do not decide translation, theology, national identity, or morality.

route.title: Watchpost transition awaiting answer
route.marker: First-person stand-set-watch resolve anticipates what will be spoken; the explicit Yahweh-answered formula starts at 2:2.
route.rationale: This liminal verse closes complaint posture and opens expectation without becoming part of the divine speech.
route.rejected: Attach 2:1 backward to 1:12-2:1 or forward to 2:1-5 and suppress its bridge function.
route.counter: The one-verse hinge is dependent on both neighboring movements and cannot interpret itself.
route.basis: Its distinct speech-act posture justifies recoverability only with mandatory 1:12-2:5 hydration.
route.guard: Never retrieve 2:1 as a free-standing watchfulness maxim; hydrate both complaint and answer.

route.title: Written-vision answer prologue and oppressor bridge
route.marker: The answer formula begins write-and-wait assurance; the proud-versus-faithful contrast and insatiable gatherer lead directly to all-these at 2:6.
route.rationale: Verse 2:5 supplies the oppressor antecedent and bridge for the nations taunt, completing the answer prologue without detaching 2:4.
route.rejected: Split 2:2-3, 2:4, and 2:5; include 2:1; or extend the unit through 2:6.
route.counter: Strong internal pressures occur at 2:3|4 and 2:4|5, and the syntax and renderings in 2:4-5 remain difficult.
route.basis: Answer continuity and the 2:5-to-2:6 antecedent outweigh semantic child seams while leaving them recorded.
route.guard: Romans, Galatians, and Hebrews are reception evidence only; do not detach 2:4 or settle faithfulness, wine or wealth, referents, or theology.

route.title: Taunt introduction and first plunder woe
route.marker: The parable and taunting-proverb formula immediately voices the first woe; debtor reversal and reciprocal plunder close at 2:8 before a WLC-family pe.
route.rationale: The introduction cannot be detached from the woe embedded in its own verse, and 2:7-8 supply that accusation its reversal.
route.rejected: Surface 2:6 as a heading alone, split accusation from reversal, or retain all 2:6-20 as one thin-pass block.
route.counter: The introduction formally governs all five woes rather than only the first.
route.basis: The same verse both frames the cycle and begins its first saying; a cycle-level parent preserves the wider function.
route.guard: Keep accusation, reversal, and 2:6-20 taunt-cycle hydration together.

route.title: Second woe: unjust household gain and wall witness
route.marker: A new woe names evil household gain, 2:10 reverses it into shame and self-harm, and the stone-and-beam witness closes before a WLC-family pe after 2:11.
route.rationale: Household self-protection, self-condemnation, and answering building materials complete one accusation-consequence movement.
route.rejected: Split 2:11 from 2:9-10 or isolate the memorable wall witness.
route.counter: The building-material witness can anticipate the blood-built-city woe that opens at 2:12.
route.basis: Its answering function resolves the household accusation before the next woe formula, so it remains with 2:9-11.
route.guard: Never surface the crying stone without the unjust-household-gain woe and full taunt parent.

route.title: Third woe: blood-built city and divine-purpose reversal
route.marker: The blood-built-city woe is answered by futile labor and the earth-filling divine-purpose result; a WLC-family samekh follows 2:14.
route.rationale: Violent construction, labor for fire, and contrasting worldwide knowledge form the accusation and its completed reversal.
route.rejected: Detach 2:14 as a positive oracle or split 2:12 from 2:13-14.
route.counter: Verse 2:14 has broad proverbial and canonical resonance and attracts independent retrieval.
route.basis: Its causal placement and contrast complete this specific woe, so positive horizon and violent premise stay together.
route.guard: Never isolate 2:14 as triumph, fulfillment, or theology apart from the blood-and-futility contrast.

route.title: Fourth woe: forced drink, exposure, returning cup, and violence
route.marker: The fourth woe opens forced drinking and exposure, 2:16 reverses the cup, and the violence-to-land-and-creatures rationale closes at 2:17 before a WLC-family samekh.
route.rationale: Manipulated intoxication, reciprocal shame, divine cup, and returning violence form a complete mirrored judgment.
route.rejected: Split 2:15-16 from 2:17 or detach the violence catalogue.
route.counter: Verse 2:17 broadens beyond the drinking image and echoes the violence formula of 2:8.
route.basis: The because-clause gives the ground for the reversal, so the broadened catalogue completes rather than starts a new unit.
route.guard: Retain accusation, reversal, human bloodshed, land and creature violence, and taunt-cycle context together.

route.title: Image critique, fifth idol woe, and temple-silence reversal
route.marker: The 2:18 image-value question and mute-idol critique precede a samekh; a fresh woe opens at 2:19 and But Yahweh reverses mute products with living temple presence at 2:20 before a pe.
route.rationale: Maker trusts mute product, wood and stone lack breath, and living presence commands silence; the semantic reversal outweighs the internal marker under the larger-unit tie rule.
route.counter: The samekh after 2:18 and new woe at 2:19 make the Hebrew split a substantial child-route dissent.
route.basis: The complete idol-to-living-presence contrast is safer for retrieval, while 2:18|19 remains an explicit non-surface relation.
route.guard: Never isolate 2:20; require both 2:18-20 and the full 2:6-20 taunt cycle.

route.title: Prayer superscription and renewal-mercy petition
route.marker: The prayer and performance superscription at 3:1 governs the direct fame-work-mercy petition at 3:2; third-person advent begins at 3:3.
route.rationale: Title and opening petition are formally distinct but safer as one recoverable prayer opening than as isolated metadata.
route.rejected: Surface 3:1 and 3:2 separately or merge the petition into 3:3-7.
route.counter: The nominal superscription and direct petition are verse-complete forms with a real 3:1|2 seam.
route.basis: Brief title plus governed petition preserve both form and retrieval context; rare performance wording selects no setting or translation.
route.guard: Hydrate under the whole prayer; Shigionoth or performance terminology is not lexical, genre-history, or boundary authority.

route.title: Theophanic advent and trembling landscape
route.marker: God-came begins advent; glory, radiance, plague, shaking earth, crumbling mountains, and trembling tents accumulate through 3:7 before a WLC-family samekh and new river questions.
route.rationale: Arrival and cosmic-national trembling form a coherent advent stanza inside the larger theophany.
route.rejected: Split at Selah inside 3:3, isolate 3:7, or retain all 3:3-15 as one surface block.
route.counter: Selah inside 3:3 and the first-person I-saw turn at 3:7 create internal stanza pressure.
route.basis: The samekh after 3:7 plus interrogative warrior turn at 3:8 is stronger than the internal Selah pressure.
route.guard: Keep prayer heading, 3:3-15 parent, and non-authorizing violence and dependence guards.

route.title: Warrior-theophany questions, deliverance march, and sea trampling
route.marker: River-and-sea questions open at 3:8; bow, cosmic response, wrathful march, and deliverance purpose reach Selah plus pe after 3:13; second-person warrior actions continue through the horses-and-sea close at 3:15.
route.rationale: The horses and sea at 3:8 and 3:15 form an inclusio, while actor, verbal chain, weapons, and combat continue across the strongest internal marker seam.
route.rejected: Surface 3:8-13 and 3:14-15 as siblings, or isolate the salvation-purpose clause.
route.counter: Selah, WLC-family pe, WEB line break, and the first-person object at 3:14 make 3:13|14 the strongest child-seam dissent in Habakkuk.
route.basis: The larger unit wins narrowly because 3:14-15 complete the same march rather than initiate a new scene; the split remains explicit dissent.
route.guard: Never isolate cosmic-warrior imagery; retain prayer, deliverance purpose, violence and ethics caution, and boundary-neutral 3:14 ketiv-qere evidence.

route.title: Embodied trembling, deprivation concession, rejoicing, and strength
route.marker: First-person bodily response returns at 3:16; the deprivation concession at 3:17 meets yet-rejoicing at 3:18 and strength, deer-foot movement, and musical subscription at 3:19.
route.rationale: Fear and waiting supply the situation, crop and herd failure the concession, and rejoicing plus strength the complete response and prayer close.
route.rejected: Split 3:16 from 3:17-19, surface 3:17-18 alone, or detach the 3:19 confession or subscription.
route.counter: The first-person return, concessive marker, emphatic response, and subscription are real internal turns.
route.basis: None is safe without the embodied-response parent; the four-verse unit preserves the even-though and yet logic and performed close.
route.guard: Never detach crop failure, joy, strength, high-place imagery, or musical direction from 3:16-19 and the full prayer.

dissents.rationale: Samekh after 2:18 and fresh woe at 2:19 support dependent children; whole 2:18-20 preserves the idol-to-living-presence reversal.
Prayer title and direct petition are distinct child forms; whole 3:1-2 prevents the brief heading from surfacing without the prayer it governs.
Selah plus pe after 3:13 supports the strongest child seam; actor, weapons, and horses-sea inclusio narrowly favor whole 3:8-15.
The watchpost may attach backward or forward syntactically; surfacing 2:1 as a hydrated bridge preserves both relations.
Hearer response and even-though-yet confession are distinct children but cannot stand safely without the full 3:16-19 response.

post_ruling_results.hebrew: zero active appeal; three marker-based child routes preserved
